product_context: Paraform (Agentic Hiring Platform) — not a Dune Security feature. Written for a design take-home exercise; source material is the exercise prompt, not an internal spec. Scoped entirely to the candidate page; broader recruiter dashboards are out of scope.
flows: Activity + context intake (log, filters, call lifecycle)
Call lifecycle: schedule (propose times / booking link) → review (per-call Para toggle + tags)
Ask Para assistant (cited Q&A + in-chat approval-gated actions)
Cross-opportunity hold (Para pauses its actions when an offer lands elsewhere)
Scored recommended opportunities (Proposed by Para AI)
key_fields: include-in-matching toggle (on / off, per context item)
context staleness flag (volatile items past threshold)
schedule-call mode (propose times / send booking link)
per-call 'use for Para AI' toggle + call tags
cross-opportunity hold state (Para-paused action, waiting on recruiter)
integrations: On-platform calls with automatic recording / transcription
Para AI matching layer (platform-wide, surfaces scored matches beyond the recruiter's own submissions)
open_questions_flagged: What is the default approval-required timeout window before escalation?
Does the candidate ever see any part of this system, or is it recruiter/Para-AI only?
How are cross-opportunity conflicts (e.g., same-company double submission) detected — real-time rule check or periodic reconciliation?
What happens to Para AI's confidence in a candidate profile when a majority of sources are excluded from matching?
Does Paraform perform any identity resolution across independently-owned recruiter profiles for the same real person, to catch duplicate submissions to the same role from different recruiters?
Can Para AI surface a match to an opportunity the recruiter hasn't chosen, and does entering it always require recruiter confirmation the same way a recruiter-initiated submission does?
Is a 60-90 day staleness threshold right for all volatile context, or should different fact types decay at different rates?
How does Para AI compute the match score shown on recommended opportunities (e.g. 8/10) — and how is it kept legible/trustworthy to recruiters?
Which state changes trigger a cross-opportunity hold (offer confirmed, offer verbal, final round scheduled?) and how long does Para hold before re-escalating?
The cross-candidate 'needs your review' backlog belongs on the home dashboard (out of scope here) — how should this feature hand off to it?
confidence_notes: Single source (the take-home prompt itself) with no existing Figma or internal spec to cross-reference. Scope, actors, and edge cases were reasonably inferable from the prompt and the linked Passive Placements concept, but several judgment calls (default visibility rules, approval timeout window, conflict-detection mechanism) are design decisions made to produce a complete PRD rather than facts confirmed by the source. Updated 2026-07-11 with further product research indicating candidate profiles are owned per recruiter (not shared platform-wide) and that Para AI's matching reach can extend beyond opportunities the recruiter has directly pursued — this is a working hypothesis pending confirmation, not a PM-confirmed fact, and is tracked as open questions. Updated again 2026-07-11 with an IA refinement from design review: Opportunities as the default landing view, Profile split from Context, Action Queue merged inline, durable-vs-volatile context staleness — these are design decisions, not externally confirmed facts. Refocused 2026-07-14 onto the candidate page only — the home/candidates-list/all-opportunities dashboards were dropped from scope — and expanded with the Activity tab (log + date/company/type filters), the on-platform call lifecycle (schedule via propose-times or booking-link sent over LinkedIn/email → post-call review with a per-call Para toggle and tags), scored recommended opportunities, the cross-opportunity hold where Para pauses its own queued actions when an offer lands elsewhere, and the Ask Para assistant (cited Q&A plus in-chat approval-gated actions). These are design decisions, not externally confirmed facts.
